note: Learning metadata only. These objects do not authorize, deny, or detect. Splunk does not enforce CTRL-INPUT-001.
path_a: TRY IT YOURSELF — construct the search in Splunk Search. Studio tokens are not the fresh LIVE run.id.
path_b: SHOW SOLUTION — copyable SPL from an existing Q-* hunt, bound table on canonical REPLAY, explanation, limitations.

investigations.title: Find the run
investigations.security_question: What evidence did this LIVE experiment generate?
investigations.learning_objective: Use run.id as the forensic correlation key. One UUID, one experiment copy.
prerequisites: a run.id from Attack Service or Investigate specimen
investigations.starter_guidance: Index agentsec_telemetry, sourcetype otel:agentic:json. Filter quoted agentsec.run.id. Do not search index=*.
investigations.hint_1: Start with index=agentsec_telemetry sourcetype=otel:agentic:json and the quoted field agentsec.run.id. Paste the LIVE run.id from Attack Service, or use the Investigate specimen REPLAY id.
investigations.hint_2: Count physical events with stats dc(_raw) as n. Do not use stats count by agentsec.run.id — duplicate JSON/OTLP field copies inflate that number.
investigations.expected_result_shape: One row per event, sorted by sequence. LIVE ATTACK (vulnerable) is typically 22 rows when Ollama completes. Defended RETEST is typically 6 rows. BASELINE is typically 22. schema_version on a restaged runtime is 1.9.0.
investigations.result_explanation: You are looking at the indexed copy of one run. sequence is the runtime order, not _time. run_id and incident_id should match.
investigations.security_interpretation: Correlation starts with run.id. Without it you mix experiments. Splunk showing rows does not mean Splunk authorized the loan.
investigations.does_not_prove: Index presence does not prove completeness, prevention, or that the attack succeeded. Empty is not SAFE.
investigations.related_control: none on this step — you are locating evidence, not judging CTRL-INPUT-001 yet

investigations.title: Reconstruct the sequence
investigations.security_question: What happened, and in what order?
investigations.learning_objective: Read event.name along sequence: start, hop, control, operation, stop, complete.
investigations.starter_guidance: Keep the same run.id filter. Sort by agentsec.sequence. Name the events: run.started, hop.started, control.decision, llm.*, pipeline.stopped, hop.completed, run.completed.
investigations.hint_1: Reuse Q-RUN-EVENTS. The event_name column is the timeline. Do not hunt session.id.
investigations.hint_2: On LIVE ATTACK (vulnerable) you should see control.decision then llm.started / llm.completed. On defended RETEST you should see control.decision then pipeline.stopped — and no llm.started. On BASELINE you should see control.decision then llm.* on each hop.
investigations.expected_result_shape: Ordered event_name list. LIVE ATTACK vulnerable: four hops of control + llm then completed_allowed. Defended RETEST: started → hop.started → control.decision → pipeline.stopped → hop.completed hop_denied → run.completed completed_denied. BASELINE: four hops of control + llm then completed_allowed.
investigations.result_explanation: sequence is assigned by AcmeBank as events are emitted. Sorting by sequence reconstructs the hop, not wall-clock jitter.
investigations.security_interpretation: The timeline shows whether the control sat before the dangerous operation. That order is a property of the runtime, copied into Splunk.
investigations.does_not_prove: A missing llm.* row in an incomplete export is not a timeline of prevention. Completeness first.
investigations.related_control: CTRL-INPUT-001 (position in the timeline, not a Splunk verdict)

investigations.title: Find the security decision
investigations.security_question: Which control evaluated the untrusted input and what decision did it make?
investigations.learning_objective: CTRL-INPUT-001 decides ALLOW or DENY at the trust boundary. Splunk did not make that decision.
investigations.starter_guidance: Filter event.name=agentsec.control.decision on the same run.id. Read control.id, decision, reason, hop.index.
investigations.hint_1: The hunt is Q-CONTROL-DECISION. Restrict to event.name=agentsec.control.decision. Do not invent a prefixed event-name field.
investigations.hint_2: On LIVE ATTACK expect hop 0 ALLOW with a fail-open reason and later executed=true on llm.* rows. On defended RETEST expect hop 0 DENY, reason input_pattern_matched, attempted=false, executed=false, outcome=prevented. On BASELINE expect four ALLOW rows with executed=false on the control event.
investigations.expected_result_shape: Control rows only. BASELINE: 4 ALLOW. LIVE ATTACK: 4 ALLOW with fail-open reason. Defended RETEST: 1 DENY hop 0.
investigations.result_explanation: decision and reason are runtime fields copied into the index. attempted/executed on this event describe the governed LLM operation at decision time, not whether Splunk agreed.
investigations.security_interpretation: AcmeBank enforced CTRL-INPUT-001 at acmebank.http_api before acmebank.llm_call. Splunk observed the copy. ALLOW is not execution.
investigations.does_not_prove: DENY by itself does not prove the model never ran. You still need execution evidence. Splunk is not the enforcement point.

investigations.title: Did execution occur?
investigations.security_question: Did the protected operation actually execute?
investigations.learning_objective: Distinguish request, decision, attempt, execution, and outcome. Runtime is authoritative for non-invocation.
investigations.starter_guidance: Search llm.started / llm.completed / llm.failed on this run.id. executed=true means the governed call began.
investigations.hint_1: The hunt is Q-LLM-EXECUTED. Filter event.name to agentsec.llm.started, agentsec.llm.completed, or agentsec.llm.failed.
investigations.hint_2: BASELINE: 8 rows (started+completed ×4), executed=true. LIVE ATTACK complete copy: 8 rows when Ollama works. Defended RETEST complete copy: zero rows. Zero Splunk rows corroborate local events.jsonl; they do not independently prove prevention.
investigations.expected_result_shape: BASELINE: 8 llm.* rows, hops 0–3. LIVE ATTACK complete copy: 8 rows, executed=true. Defended RETEST complete copy: 0 rows.
investigations.result_explanation: llm.started with executed=true means Ollama generate began. llm.completed outcome=success is completion, not loan approval. llm.failed is invocation then error, not DENY.
investigations.security_interpretation: Prevention is DENY before invoke plus no llm.started in a complete runtime pack. Splunk absence is corroboration only.
investigations.does_not_prove: Missing llm.* is not blocked, SAFE, or prevented if export was incomplete. Do not treat empty Splunk as the control.

investigations.title: BASELINE vs ATTACK
investigations.security_question: What changed between the normal and adversarial specimen?
investigations.learning_objective: Compare evidence, not stories. Do not label BASELINE SAFE.
investigations.starter_guidance: Compare two run.ids: benign ATK-001 vs ATK-002. Hold the hunt constant (Q-CONTROL-DECISION or Q-LLM-EXECUTED). Change only the run.id.
investigations.hint_1: Path A: launch BASELINE then ATTACK on Attack Service, copy both run.ids, run the same hunt twice in Search. Then launch RETEST for the closed loop. Path B tables on this tab are canonical REPLAY ids, not your fresh LIVE ids.
investigations.hint_2: SAME: app, schema, CTRL-INPUT-001 placement. DIFFERENT: input string and therefore hop-0 decision / whether llm.* exists. BASELINE is not SAFE — it is the normal shape.
investigations.expected_result_shape: REPLAY COMPARE: BASELINE 4 ALLOW + 8 llm.*. LIVE ATTACK 4 ALLOW fail-open + 8 llm.*. Defended RETEST 1 DENY + 0 llm.*. Fingerprint equality is measured on content hash, not specimen name.
investigations.result_explanation: You are comparing two experiment copies. Empty COMPARE tables mean those canonical ids are not on this Splunk volume — not DENY.
investigations.security_interpretation: The experimental variable is untrusted input reaching CTRL-INPUT-001. Profile decides DENY vs labeled fail-open. Splunk records both; it authorizes neither.
investigations.does_not_prove: BASELINE is not SAFE. Vulnerable ALLOW is not loan approval. Defended DENY still needs execution evidence before you claim prevention.

investigations.title: What can you prove?
investigations.security_question: Which statements are supported by this evidence, corroborated, not proven, or incorrect?
investigations.learning_objective: Classify claims. DENY is not proof of non-execution by itself. Splunk is not enforcement.
investigations.starter_guidance: For each statement below, pick: SUPPORTED BY EVIDENCE, CORROBORATED, NOT PROVEN, or INCORRECT. Tie the answer to a field or a pack file.
investigations.hint_1: SUPPORTED needs a runtime or complete indexed field. CORROBORATED is Splunk agreeing with a complete local copy. NOT PROVEN is a gap. INCORRECT contradicts the evidence model.
investigations.hint_2: Refresh: DENY != proof of non-execution by itself; missing event != blocked; Splunk != enforcement; untrusted != malicious; HEC success != searchable evidence.
investigations.expected_result_shape: Classification exercise. Q-LLM-AFTER-DENY on a complete defended ATTACK copy is 0 rows — corroboration, not independent prevention proof. The SIMULATED makeresults row is not OBSERVED runtime.
investigations.result_explanation: Q-LLM-AFTER-DENY asks whether llm.* followed DENY on the same hop. Zero rows on a complete copy means that sequence was not indexed. The positive-control table is SIMULATED.
investigations.security_interpretation: You can prove what the complete evidence says. You cannot promote gaps, HEC 200, or Studio rendering into prevention.
investigations.does_not_prove: This workshop does not prove INV-008 for paraphrases, production authn, or other labs. Zero detection rows are not a shipped detector.

investigations.title: ATTACK vs RETEST
investigations.security_question: What changed between ATTACK and RETEST?
investigations.learning_objective: Prove SAME adversarial input, DIFFERENT server-owned defense, DIFFERENT outcome. Splunk observed; Splunk did not cause it.
investigations.starter_guidance: Use the LIVE RUN PAIR from Attack Service. Path A: run Q-CONTROL-DECISION and Q-LLM-EXECUTED twice, once per run.id. Path B: canonical REPLAY tables on COMPARE. Measure the input fingerprint; do not trust fixture names.
investigations.hint_1: SAME: ATK-002 payload, content hash, CTRL-INPUT-001 placement. DIFFERENT: experiment_id, security.profile, testbed.mode, hop-0 decision, llm.* presence.
investigations.hint_2: Authoritative: runtime hop attempted/executed. Control evidence: decision+reason. Corroborative: complete Splunk copy. Not sufficient alone: missing event, DENY string, HEC 200, empty dashboard, pytest.
investigations.expected_result_shape: ATTACK: 4 ALLOW fail-open + llm.* when Ollama works. RETEST: 1 DENY hop 0 + 0 llm.* on a complete copy. Fingerprints match. run.ids differ.
investigations.result_explanation: The experimental variable is the server-owned ExperimentContext. The input fingerprint must match. Empty COMPARE tables on canonical ids mean those UUIDs are not on this volume.
investigations.security_interpretation: AcmeBank changed the outcome by using a different experiment configuration. Splunk reconstructed both copies. Splunk did not ALLOW or DENY.
investigations.does_not_prove: RETEST is not automatically SAFE. DENY is not universal prompt-injection resistance. Missing telemetry is not prevention.
